long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Abdullah's environmental work addresses Bahrain's exposure to rising seas. He has advocated including climate risks in development plans and called for international finance and technology transfer to support emissions reductions. His responsibilities at the Supreme Council for Environment also encompass wildlife and marine protection, linking climate policy with the conservation of natural resources.

In 2006, he entered a recording partnership with Michael Jackson through Two Seas Records. The venture appointed British music executive Guy Holmes as chief executive and announced plans for a new Jackson album the following year.
